title: POC weekly sync - throughput optim
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on throughput tuning. Reviewed latest bench results after continuous batching changes, discussed target concurrency and queueing behavior, identified two regressions in 99th pct latency under peak load, agreed to test updated batching policy and run a 2-hour soak with higher concurrency. Next steps: send updated perf spreadsheet, run longer soak, share queuing config, confirm success criteria for production cutover.
topics: continuous batching adjustments, concurrency targets, queueing/backpressure, 99th pct latency, GPU utilization, KV/prefix caching, load patterns (burst vs steady), soak tests, rollout plan
transcript:
00:00 Alex: hey everyone good morning, uh we're gonna keep this tight 45 min, quick recap then dive into the numbers.
00:14 Maya: thanks Alex, appreciate it. Samir is on for the perf stuff.
00:21 Priya: hi all, so for context we ran the new continuous batching patch on two nodes last night, configs are in the sheet link that Alex sent, basically bumped batch window to 10ms and increased target batch size to 16.
00:35 Samir: yeah i pulled the spreadsheet, quick note the aggregate throughput jumped about 28% at steady state which is great but we saw tail latency creep during the burst tests, the 99th went from 420ms to about 780ms under 2x traffic.
00:51 Alex: okay that's the key tradeoff, throughput up but tail latency hurt, can you confirm this was with KV cache warm?
01:03 Samir: kv cache mostly warm, some cold starts in the test ramp, also we had a higher concurrency cap of 48 which may have increased queueing.
01:16 Priya: right, the continuous batching favors packing requests which increases GPU utilization but if concurrency hits the queue threshold then we see head-of-line queuing and those outliers.
01:30 Lena: just to be clear our SLO is 95% < 200ms and 99% < 600ms for the customer-facing route, so 780ms is above that, we need a plan.
01:45 Alex: understood. quick question, are we seeing model stalls or kernel contention on the GPU? Priya: from the traces the avg GPU util is 86% and there are short spikes, but CPU side the worker pool threads get starved briefly, maybe kernel launch queuing.
02:03 Samir: also worth noting network jitter during ramp contributed a few ms, transcript shows some jitter but not the main cause.
02:14 Maya: what are our options? lower target batch size, reduce concurrency, add backpressure queueing?
02:23 Priya: options: 1) reduce batch window to 6ms and cap batch size to 12 to reduce packing latency for small requests. 2) enforce concurrency target of 32 for the route and allow overflow to a secondary pool (dedicated slower GPUs) 3) add adaptive queueing so long requests get deprioritized.
02:43 Alex: can we simulate option 2 quickly in the sandbox? i.e. enforce concurrency 32 and overflow to pool-b with a slightly cheaper model variant.
02:54 Priya: yes we can, we have pool-b ready but need to update routing policy JSON, it's small change. Samir, can you run a 30 minute soak with concurrency=32 and batch window=10ms so we isolate concurrency effect?
03:09 Samir: i can run that right after the call. i also want to replicate the exact burst profile the customer saw, do you have the ingress histogram?
03:18 Maya: yes, shared in the slack channel finite-edge-ingress.csv, it's the 2x burst at 1m intervals.
03:27 Alex: perfect. quick note on metrics — please check GPU queue lengths and worker thread histograms as priya mentioned, those will show head-of-line queueing.
03:40 Priya: another observation: prefix cache hit rate was 92% for the test but some mid-requests had cache misses leading to 2x KV load paths and spikes. improving warmup will help.
03:55 Samir: hmm ok, we can do a warmup pass before the soak to push prefix cache to 99%, that should reduce cold-start tails.
04:05 Lena: is there any chance this is model specific? we are running the 13B open variant right?
04:13 Priya: yes 13B quantized q4_0, kernel selection seems fine. we did notice the attention kernel has slightly worse perf at 2048 sequence lengths in the open variant; for short requests it's fine.
04:26 Samir: so most of the tails are from larger sequence requests during bursts, maybe the routing policy can shard by seq length.
04:35 Alex: good thought. could we route >512 tokens to pool-b automatically?
04:40 Priya: yes, we can add that rule, low-effort change.
04:45 Maya: that seems reasonable, we don't expect many >512 but during bursts we saw a handful.
04:52 Alex: ok let’s capture the action items. also i want to call out one regression we saw last week after increasing concurrent worker threads — there was a memory bump on node-3, could be a leak.
05:06 Priya: we looked at it, likely due to stale KV entries not being evicted, i have a patch to add TTL eviction.
05:15 Samir: i'll include memory graphs in the sheet.
05:21 Priya: for the soak plan: run with concurrency=32, batch_window=10ms, batch_size_target=16, warmup run to push prefix KV to 99%, route >512 tokens to pool-b, monitor 50/95/99/99.9 latencies and GPU queue length.
05:37 Maya: timeline?
05:40 Alex: can we have the soak results within 24 hours? Samir: yes i'll kick off today and share results by tomorrow 10am PT.
05:50 Lena: if the soak looks good what's next?
05:54 Alex: plan for a 2-hour production-like soak at 2x traffic with gradual ramp and circuit-breaker thresholds, if that passes we'll evaluate canary rollout to 10% traffic.
06:07 Priya: also we'll provide a suggested rollout config with concurrency targets per route and a fallback to hosted model variants if pool saturation occurs.
06:18 Samir: one more thing, i noticed the per-token cost improved ~18% with the batching changes, so there's a solid cost upside if we can get tail latency under control.
06:30 Maya: good, cost matters. can you add cost per 1M tokens to the sheet?
06:35 Alex: will do.
06:38 (crosstalk)
07:00 Alex: quick Q from sales: any security blockers from private/hosted split? Maya: we need remote logging redaction and SOC2 evidence for the route.
07:12 Priya: we can enable redaction and share SOC2 summary, will attach to the doc.
07:20 Lena: ok thanks.
07:25 Alex: let's recap: Samir to run 30min soak with concurrency=32 and warmup, then 2-hour soak if results look ok; Priya to push TTL eviction and routing-by-length rule; Alex to update perf sheet and send suggested rollout and cost calc; Maya to confirm SOC2 doc request.
07:48 Samir: i'll also log any OOMs or mem growth and tag the timestamps in the trace.
08:00 Alex: cool, we'll reconvene next week same time. anything else?
08:07 Maya: nope, thanks all.
08:10 Alex: thanks, bye.
